comparisons.comparison: Both GS (GSBE) and BAC (BofASE) disclose capital requirements for their European bank subsidiaries supervised by the ECB. GSBE is subject to standalone regulatory capital requirements under EU CRD/CRR (Basel III-based), while BofASE is supervised by the ECB and subject to minimum Pillar 1 capital requirements. A key difference is the level of specific capital detail: BAC provides specific dollar amounts for capital resources ($10.9 billion) and the minimum Pillar 1 requirement ($3.3 billion) for BofASE, whereas GS's disclosure for GSBE describes the regulatory framework and deposit protection programs without providing specific capital resource figures or Pillar 1 requirements in the cited text.

sentences.text: • GSBE. GSBE is our German bank subsidiary supervised by the European Central Bank, BaFin and Deutsche Bundesbank. GSBE is a non-U.S. banking subsidiary of GS Bank USA and is also subject to standalone regulatory capital requirements noted below. GSBE is subject to the capital requirements prescribed in the amended E.U. Capital Requirements Directive (CRD) and E.U. Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR), which are largely based on Basel III. The deposits of GSBE are covered by the German statutory deposit protection program to the extent provided by law. In addition, GSBE has elected to participate in the German voluntary deposit protection program which provides further insurance for certain eligible deposits beyond the coverage of the German statutory deposit program.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory Framework and Basel III Implementation
comparisons.peer_summary: J.P. Morgan SE is regulated by the ECB and German authorities, and is subject to EU capital requirements under Basel III, with final standards becoming effective on January 1, 2025 (except market risk aspects effective January 1, 2026).
comparisons.comparison: Both GS (GSBE) and JPM (JPMSE) disclose regulatory capital requirements for their major German bank subsidiaries, which are supervised by the ECB and German authorities (BaFin/Bundesbank) and subject to EU capital requirements based on Basel III. A key similarity is the explicit link to Basel III standards. A key difference is the timing of implementation for final Basel III standards: JPMSE notes these became effective January 1, 2025 (with market risk in 2026), whereas GSBE's disclosure focuses on its current status under the amended CRD/CRR without specifying the exact effective date of the 'final' standards in the same sentence, though it notes participation in German deposit protection programs.

sentences.text: • GSBE. GSBE is our German bank subsidiary supervised by the European Central Bank, BaFin and Deutsche Bundesbank. GSBE is a non-U.S. banking subsidiary of GS Bank USA and is also subject to standalone regulatory capital requirements noted below. GSBE is subject to the capital requirements prescribed in the amended E.U. Capital Requirements Directive (CRD) and E.U. Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR), which are largely based on Basel III. The deposits of GSBE are covered by the German statutory deposit protection program to the extent provided by law. In addition, GSBE has elected to participate in the German voluntary deposit protection program which provides further insurance for certain eligible deposits beyond the coverage of the German statutory deposit program.

JPMSE is regulated by the European Central Bank ("ECB"), the German Financial Supervisory Authority and the German Central Bank, as well as the local regulators in each of the countries in which it operates, and it is subject to EU capital requirements under Basel III.
Those standards became effective beginning on January 1, 2025, with the exception of market risk aspects for which the effective date is January 1, 2026.
